I thought it might be useful to start a thread discussing relation algebras, for which I have opened a first PR cslib#1127. This is a somewhat niche area at the intersection of logic, computer science, and combinatorics, so maybe a bit of explanation is helpful or just interesting to share with others.

The simple idea is to have an algebraic description of binary relations. You can imagine for instance the Boolean algebra of all binary relations on a given set (the type α → α → Prop in Lean), along with the monoid that is characterized by their composition and the converse operation. Tarski developed a set of equations meant to capture this idea. For Boolean algebra there is the Stone representation theorem, so the idea was meant to be that any type satisfying these should have an isomorphism with binary relations. This turns out to fail spectacularly. Not only are there very small relation algebras that are not representable, but it turns out that the class of all representable relation algebras has no finite axiomatization.

With this is mind, a question of interest in this subfield is characterizing and classifying which relation algebras are representable. This turns out to have connections to computer science problems like constraint satisfaction or questions about graph coloring. I'd like to develop the theory of relation algebras in CSLib to the point that we are able to formalize some of these connections, along with some of the statements of open conjectures in the field (see for instance On the Future of RA).

Partially as a sanity check and partially due to general interest, I've also formalized the number of relation algebras up to isomorphism for integral relation algebras with six or fewer atoms (and have progress on seven, which numbers in the billions, see List of small integral relation algebras). For the small ones where it is fully known (up to 4 atoms) I have fully constructed and classified as representable or nonrepresentable. My interest here was to see how AI would do with my relatively naive prompting about crafting representations for efficient kernel proofs. I was quite surprised here, as without explicit instructions to do so Astra took a Pascal script from the 90s and converted this to a C++ calculation that is then checked by Lean. Rest assured that I am only upsteaming and carefully manually reviewing the core definitions of relation algebras that are needed to establish the theory and once this is done (it will take a series a PRs) will place all this calculation-heavy development in a downstream repo.

Binary relations with union as +, composition as *, and transitive closure as Kleene star form a Kleene algebra:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kleene_algebra
https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Kleene.html#KleeneAlgebra
Kleene algebra does have a finite axiomatization (see the Wikipedia article above).

The only place I know where some of this has been formalized (in Rocq) is https://perso.ens-lyon.fr/damien.pous/ra/, but I think it doesn't cover any of the theory of representations I'm interested in.

The definition of representation is cslib#Cslib.RelationAlgebra.Representation, which is defined as an embedding into a product of relations. This is equivalent (and appears in the literature) but I think less common than characterizing in terms of proper relation algebras. We should have this, so here is my rough sketch for feedback before I start putting together a PR. First, we should define subalgebras:

import Cslib
import Mathlib.Order.BooleanSubalgebra

structure RelationSubalgebra [Cslib.RelationAlgebra α] extends BooleanSubalgebra α, Submonoid α where
  star_mem' {a : α} : a ∈ carrier → star a ∈ carrier -- not sure if there's a Mathlib class for this line...

Intuitively what we would like is the relation algebra on subsets of relations but as @Thomas Waring pointed out to me we can't just directly use RelationSubalgebra because this needs to be relative to an equivalence relation that serves as the unit. So we should define

-- is this bundling the right thing to do??
-- naming??
structure FullRelationAlgebra (s : Setoid β) where
  val : SetRel β β
  subset_unit : val ⊆ {(a, b) | s a b} -- not in Mathlib, should be its own `def`?

A proper relation algebra is then just RelationSubalgebra (FullRelationAlgebra s), and we can show that:

  • being representable is equivalent to an embedding into such a subalgebra
  • RelationAlgebraEquiv (SquareRelations α) (FullRelationAlgebra (⊤ : Setoid α))

(i’m on mobile right now so i’ll write it out properly later) i think if you relax the definition of homomorphism to not require preserving top then you can just require an injective map into the full algebra of (conventional) relations — the important part is that it’s an order embedding and preserves the composition and star, so that the RA operations are “represented” by the SetRel versions
that ought to give as a corollary that the image of top is an equivalence relation — requiring that explicitly seems a little awkward
Hmm, this seems rather awkward to me, but I'll wait for details to see if I've misunderstood. (No rush at all)
I do agree about it being odd to specify the equivalence relation though, I'm just failing to find a nice way around it.

here's a rough outline of an alternative version of "representation" — the idea is that you don't try to define a RelationAlgebra which is some subset of SetRel X X (or your SquareRelations X), but just look at the function into SetRel X X from your original relation algebra. that function should be injective, and preserve all of the RA operations with the possible exception of the complement / top, which is relaxed to just preserving the sdiff

i think this faithfully captures the literature definition of representation, but if there's a particular result i could prove to validate that let me know

representation

import Cslib.Foundations.RelationAlgebra.Representation

open Relation

namespace Cslib.RelationAlgebra

variable {α β : Type*} [RelationAlgebra α]

abbrev SquareRelations.toSetRel (r : SquareRelations β) : SetRel β β := r

abbrev SquareRelations.toRel (r : SquareRelations β) (x y : β) : Prop := (x, y) ∈ r.toSetRel

structure Representation' (α β : Type*) [RelationAlgebra α] extends
    α →⋆* (SquareRelations β), α ↪o (SquareRelations β),
    LatticeHom α (SquareRelations β) where
  map_sdiff (a b : α) : toFun (a \ b) = toFun a \ toFun b

namespace Representation'

instance : FunLike (Representation' α β) α (SquareRelations β) where
  coe f := f.toFun
  coe_injective f g h := by
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := f
    obtain ⟨⟨⟨⟨_, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩, _⟩ := g
    congr

lemma mono (f : Representation' α β) {a b : α} (h : a ≤ b) : f a ≤ f b :=
  f.map_rel_iff.mpr h

lemma map_compl (f : Representation' α β) (a : α) : f aᶜ = f ⊤ \ f a := by
  rw [← top_sdiff]
  exact f.map_sdiff ⊤ a

theorem equivalence_map_top (f : Representation' α β) : Equivalence (f ⊤).toRel where
  refl a := by
    suffices (1 : SquareRelations β) ≤ f ⊤ from this <| SetRel.mem_id.mpr rfl
    rw [← f.map_one]
    exact f.mono le_top
  symm {a b} h := by
    suffices star (f ⊤) ≤ f ⊤ from this <| SetRel.mem_inv.mpr h
    convert! ← f.mono (@le_top α _ _ (star ⊤))
    exact f.map_star' ⊤
  trans {a b c} h h' := by
    suffices (f ⊤) * (f ⊤) ≤ f ⊤ from this <| SetRel.prodMk_mem_comp h h'
    convert! ← f.mono (@le_top α _ _ (⊤ * ⊤))
    exact f.map_mul ⊤ ⊤

end Representation'

end Cslib.RelationAlgebra

sounds good, i'm definitely not certain the way i suggested is any better — if you / we do go down the path of defining the codomain of the representation (ie the down-closure of an equivalence relation inside SetRel) then i think the right way to go about it would be to do the same construction for any relation algebra. you can define what it means to be an equivalence relation in any RA, and i think for any such x Set.Iic x should be an RA: the mul and star come from the equivalence relation as:

Set.Iic instances

import Cslib.Foundations.RelationAlgebra.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Monoid.Unbundled.Basic

namespace Cslib.RelationAlgebra

variable {α : Type*} [RelationAlgebra α]

instance : MulLeftMono α where
  elim x y z h := by
    simp only [← sup_eq_left] at h ⊢
    rw [← mul_sup, h]

instance : MulRightMono α where
  elim x y z h := by
    simp only [← sup_eq_left] at h ⊢
    rw [← sup_mul, h]

lemma le_star_iff {x y : α} : x ≤ star y ↔ star x ≤ y := by
  have h (x y : α) (h : x ≤ star y) : star x ≤ y := by
    convert star_mono h
    simp
  refine ⟨h x y, by simpa using h (star x) (star y)⟩

class IsRefl (x : α) where
  one_le : 1 ≤ x

class IsSymm (x : α) where
  star_eq : star x = x

lemma isSymm_of_star_le {x : α} (h : star x ≤ x) : IsSymm x where
  star_eq := h.antisymm (le_star_iff.mpr h)

lemma star_le_of_isSymm {x y : α} [IsSymm y] (h : x ≤ y) : star x ≤ y := by
  rw [← IsSymm.star_eq (x := y)]
  exact star_mono h

class IsTrans (x : α) where
  mul_self_le : x * x ≤ x

lemma mul_le_of_isTrans {x y z : α} [IsTrans z] (hx : x ≤ z) (hy : y ≤ z) : x * y ≤ z :=
  (mul_le_mul' hx hy).trans IsTrans.mul_self_le

instance (x : α) [IsRefl x] : One (Set.Iic x) where
  one := ⟨1, IsRefl.one_le⟩

instance (x : α) [IsTrans x] : Semigroup (Set.Iic x) where
  mul a b := ⟨a * b, mul_le_of_isTrans a.property b.property⟩
  mul_assoc a b c := by ext; exact mul_assoc (a : α) b c

instance (x : α) [IsRefl x] [IsTrans x] : Monoid (Set.Iic x) where
  one_mul a := by ext; exact one_mul (a : α)
  mul_one a := by ext; exact mul_one (a : α)

instance (x : α) [IsSymm x] : InvolutiveStar (Set.Iic x) where
  star a := ⟨star a, star_le_of_isSymm a.property⟩
  star_involutive a := by ext; exact star_involutive (a : α)

instance (x : α) [IsSymm x] [IsTrans x] : StarMul (Set.Iic x) where
  star_mul a b := by ext; exact star_mul (a : α) b

ok the whole instance is here, there are some pure order lemmas which should be split out etc but it works as a proof of concept

RelationAlgebra (Set.Iic x)

import Cslib.Foundations.RelationAlgebra.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Monoid.Unbundled.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.LatticeIntervals

namespace Cslib.RelationAlgebra

variable {α : Type*} [RelationAlgebra α]

instance : MulLeftMono α where
  elim x y z h := by simp_all [← sup_eq_left, ← mul_sup]

instance : MulRightMono α where
  elim x y z h := by simp_all [← sup_eq_left, ← sup_mul]

lemma le_star_iff {x y : α} : x ≤ star y ↔ star x ≤ y := by
  have h (x y : α) (h : x ≤ star y) : star x ≤ y := by
    simpa using star_mono h
  refine ⟨h x y, by simpa using h (star x) (star y)⟩

class IsRefl (x : α) where
  one_le : 1 ≤ x

class IsSymm (x : α) where
  star_eq : star x = x

lemma isSymm_of_star_le {x : α} (h : star x ≤ x) : IsSymm x where
  star_eq := h.antisymm (le_star_iff.mpr h)

lemma star_le_of_isSymm {x y : α} [IsSymm y] (h : x ≤ y) : star x ≤ y := by
  rw [← IsSymm.star_eq (x := y)]
  exact star_mono h

class IsTrans (x : α) where
  mul_self_le : x * x ≤ x

lemma mul_le_of_isTrans {x y z : α} [IsTrans z] (hx : x ≤ z) (hy : y ≤ z) : x * y ≤ z :=
  (mul_le_mul' hx hy).trans IsTrans.mul_self_le

instance (x : α) [IsRefl x] : One (Set.Iic x) where
  one := ⟨1, IsRefl.one_le⟩

instance (x : α) [IsTrans x] : Semigroup (Set.Iic x) where
  mul a b := ⟨a * b, mul_le_of_isTrans a.property b.property⟩
  mul_assoc a b c := by ext; exact mul_assoc (a : α) b c

instance (x : α) [IsRefl x] [IsTrans x] : Monoid (Set.Iic x) where
  one_mul a := by ext; exact one_mul (a : α)
  mul_one a := by ext; exact mul_one (a : α)

instance (x : α) [IsSymm x] : InvolutiveStar (Set.Iic x) where
  star a := ⟨star a, star_le_of_isSymm a.property⟩
  star_involutive a := by ext; exact star_involutive (a : α)

instance (x : α) [IsSymm x] [IsTrans x] : StarMul (Set.Iic x) where
  star_mul a b := by ext; exact star_mul (a : α) b

instance (β : Type*) [GeneralizedCoheytingAlgebra β] (x : β) : SDiff (Set.Iic x) where
  sdiff a b := ⟨a \ b, sdiff_le.trans a.prop⟩

instance instGeneralizedBooleanAlgebraIic (β : Type*) [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra β] (x : β) :
    GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra (Set.Iic x) :=
  Subtype.coe_injective.generalizedBooleanAlgebra (f := fun (a : Set.Iic x) ↦ (a : β)) Iff.rfl
    Iff.rfl (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) (fun _ _ ↦ rfl) rfl (fun _ _ ↦ rfl)

instance instBooleanAlgebraIic (β : Type*) [GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra β] (x : β) :
  BooleanAlgebra (Set.Iic x) := GeneralizedBooleanAlgebra.toBooleanAlgebra

lemma inf_mul_le {a b c : α} : a * (b ⊓ c) ≤ a * b ⊓ a * c :=
  le_inf (mul_le_mul_right inf_le_left a) (mul_le_mul_right inf_le_right a)

attribute [gcongr] star_mono

instance instRelationAlgebraIic (x : α) [IsRefl x] [IsSymm x] [IsTrans x] :
    RelationAlgebra (Set.Iic x) where
  sup_mul a b c := by ext; exact sup_mul (a : α) b c
  star_sup a b := by ext; exact star_sup (a : α) b
  tarski a b := by
    change star (a : α) * (x \ (a * b)) ≤ x \ b
    grw [sdiff_eq, sdiff_eq, inf_mul_le, tarski, (show a ≤ x from a.prop),
      IsSymm.star_eq, IsTrans.mul_self_le]

Thanks for the details Thomas, I'll consider this more carefully. I'm now up to what I'd consider a first relatively short (~2000 lines, much of it general background) but non-trivial theorem about representations that can serve as a good test of definitions. With AI-assistance, I've completed Monk's proof that there is no finite axiomatization of representable relation algebras. I expect it'll take me at least a few weeks to slowly clean this up.

To me this shows the value of us being downstream of Mathlib: to my knowledge nobody has formalized this previously, and my guess as to why is that it'd be quite a pain to setup all the prerequisites from scratch. You need to characterize the non-representability of a family of relation algebras of projective lines, then translate everything into a first order language and show you get a contradiction by Łoś's theorem when you take the ultraproduct. I think many of the elements exist in Isabelle for instance, but I would find it painful to assemble without Mathlib's centralization. (Perhaps for an autoformalization this is now easy, but I still consider it important to have a more carefully designed version that can go in CSLib)

One other small design note. I've opened a Mathlib PR #45154 to scope some pointwise instances on Set. With this I think we could do away with the SquareRelations type synonym.
